parts.title: The plastic-free month
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
Last January, my sister Anna and I decided to try something new: a month without single-use plastic. We were shocked when we looked inside our kitchen. Almost everything, from the fruit to the washing-up liquid, was wrapped in plastic.

The first week was the hardest. We had to find a shop that sold loose vegetables, and we walked two kilometres to get there. We also took our own bags and jars. The man at the market looked surprised when I asked him to put olives in my jar, but he smiled and did it.

By the second week, it was easier. We learned to make our own bread and yoghurt, which tasted much better than the shop's. We also gave up plastic bottles and started to carry a metal one. My friends laughed at first, but then two of them copied us.

At the end of the month, we weighed our rubbish. It was only one small bag, compared with five bags in December. We have not become perfect, but we now think carefully before we buy anything.

questions.prompt: Why were the sisters shocked?
options: Most of their food had plastic around it
Their kitchen was very untidy then
The local shops were closed in January
questions.explanation: Almost everything was wrapped in plastic.

questions.prompt: What was difficult in the first week?
options: Finding a shop with loose vegetables
Carrying all their shopping home by bus
Making bread without using a recipe
questions.explanation: They had to walk two kilometres to find loose vegetables.

questions.prompt: How did the market man react?
options: He refused to use her jar
He gave her the olives for free
questions.explanation: He looked surprised but smiled and did it.

questions.prompt: What happened with the writer's friends?
options: All of them stopped talking to her
Two of them copied the sisters
questions.explanation: Two friends copied the metal bottle idea.

questions.prompt: What was the result at the end of the month?
options: They spent a lot more money on food
They no longer used any plastic at all
Their rubbish had become much smaller
questions.explanation: They had only one small bag of rubbish.

parts.title: A school that recycles
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
Greenfield School has become famous in our town for the way that it deals with its rubbish. [1] Two years ago, a group of students asked their headteacher to do something about the problem, and she agreed at once.

First, they put special bins in every classroom. [2] Each bin has a different colour, so that nobody gets confused, even the youngest children.

The students also made posters for the corridors. [3] The result was that more people began to take part.

The school now makes its own compost from food waste. [4] The vegetables grown there are served in the canteen at lunchtime. [5] Visitors from other schools often come to see how it works.
sentences: They are used for paper, plastic and tins.
Before that, almost all the rubbish went into one big bin.
The school canteen is open from twelve until two.
It is spread on the garden at the back of the building.
They showed what could be recycled and what could not.
The headteacher is very proud of what has been achieved.

gaps.explanation: "Before that" explains the situation two years ago.
"They" refers to the special bins, and the colours are described next.
The posters showed what could be recycled, which leads to more people taking part.
The compost is spread on the garden, and the vegetables grown there follow.
The headteacher's pride leads to visitors coming to see it.

parts.title: A talk about the recycling centre
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note with one word.

turns.speaker: martin
turns.text: Hello, everyone, and thanks for coming to the new recycling centre. I'm Martin, the manager. The centre is open from eight in the morning until six in the evening, from Monday to Saturday. It is closed on Sundays. Entry is free for local people, but you will need to show a bill with your address. There are separate containers for glass, paper, metal and plastic. Garden waste goes in the large blue skip near the entrance. We also take old electrical items, such as televisions and fridges, but we cannot accept paint. Last year, we collected over four hundred tonnes of paper. If you want more information, visit our website, or ring the office on the number on the sign.

gaps.explanation: You will need to show a bill with your address.

parts.title: An environmental volunteer
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: gerard
turns.text: My guest today is Jenna Wells, who organises clean-ups on beaches. Jenna, how did you get started?

turns.speaker: jenna
turns.text: I was walking on a beach with my grandfather, and he pointed to the rubbish. He said, 'It was clean when I was young.' I felt I had to do something.

turns.speaker: gerard
turns.text: How many people take part?

turns.speaker: jenna
turns.text: At first, there were only four of us. Now, we have about two hundred volunteers every month, which is wonderful.

turns.speaker: gerard
turns.text: What is the strangest thing you have found?

turns.speaker: jenna
turns.text: A whole sofa! Nobody knows how it got there. We also found a lot of old shoes, mostly on one foot.

turns.speaker: gerard
turns.text: Is it a hard job?

turns.speaker: jenna
turns.text: The work is tiring, but not difficult. The worst part is the smell on warm days, to be honest.

turns.speaker: gerard
turns.text: What do you do with the rubbish?

turns.speaker: jenna
turns.text: We sort it carefully. About half of it can be recycled, and the rest goes to the town tip.

turns.speaker: gerard
turns.text: What message would you give to our listeners?

turns.speaker: jenna
turns.text: Think before you throw something away. Small changes, like carrying a bottle, make a difference when many people do them.
